chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
About the man who writes to a man from the greats of the workers of the Magians, so he begins with his name before his own name, so he (peace be upon him) said:
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to prioritize a non-Muslim official's name in correspondence for practical benefit?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the principle of *al-maslaha* (public interest) in social interactions, permitting the Muslim to yield honor to a Zimmī official to secure a specific benefit. It reflects the pragmatic flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in managing relations with non-Muslim subjects under Islamic rule, prioritizing utility over rigid hierarchical etiquette.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who writes to a man from the greats ones he works for from the Magians. So he begins by his name before his own name. So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘There is no problem when he does that to choose the benefit’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Isma’il ibn Marrar from Yunus from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)

who has said the following: “The Imam was asked about the case of a man who writes to a chief officer of Majus and begins with the name of the chief before his own name. The Imam said, ‘It is permissible if it is for seeking favors.’”
